FINAL RESULT — Natural-language hypothesis answering the question:

"During the Younger Bronze Age (1100–500 BCE), the principal-component value of PC1 from the PCA on the forms of capital (12 Z-scores of symbolic, social, cultural and economic capital over 100-year slices) is at its peak at the very beginning of the period: PC1 at 1100 BCE (+4.51, the YBA maximum) is markedly HIGHER than at every subsequent horizon of 1000–500 BCE. All later slices fall below it (1000: +2.18, 900: +1.65, 800: +1.92, 700: +1.24, 600: +0.81, 500: +0.79), and from that start PC1 declines across the 1000–500 block (block mean +1.43, median +1.44; linear trend about −0.29 per century). The difference between the beginning and the block is large: PC1(1100) is roughly +3.1 above the mean (and +2.3 vs the next slice at 1000 up to +3.7 vs 500). The conclusion is robust across fit windows (full 39-slice and YBA-only 7-slice fits: in both, 1100 BCE is the highest and 1000–500 declines) and across standardization (center-only PC1 correlates r≈0.997; PC1(1100)=+4.45). This directional claim is also sign-invariant: 1100 BCE is the YBA extremum of PC1, i.e., a pronounced spike in the capital-form PC1 at the onset of the Younger Bronze Age followed by a sustained drop."

Key reported numbers (default protocol: standardized PCA on capital.csv's 39 hundred-year slices, SVD, PC1 oriented so positive loadings = capital intensity, e.g., CopperGold +0.41, Depot +0.34, PotteryDecoration +0.38; PC1 explains 30.3% of variance):
- PC1: 1100 BCE = +4.5056; 1000 = +2.1761; 900 = +1.6487; 800 = +1.9191; 700 = +1.2413; 600 = +0.8104; 500 = +0.7888
- Pairwise differences PC1(1100) − PC1(t): vs 1000 +2.33, 900 +2.86, 800 +2.59, 700 +3.26, 600 +3.70, 500 +3.72 (all positive)
- PC1(1100) − block mean(1000–500)=+3.0749; vs median +3.0606; 1100 > max(later)=+2.1761 (1100 is the YBA maximum; YBA min +0.79 at 500 BCE)
- Trend within 1000–500: slope −0.2894 per 100 years (declining)
- Sensitivities: center-only PC1(1100)=+4.4519 (corr 0.9974); YBA-only 7-slice fit PC1(1100)=+5.7779, 1000–500 range −0.03…−2.27 (1100 still the maximum, declining trend); capital.csv Z-values == time_series *_inter at slice years (0 mismatches)

payload.hypothesis: In the PCA on the forms of capital over hundred-year time slices, PC1 is at its Younger Bronze Age maximum at the onset (1100 BCE, +4.51) and is markedly higher than at every subsequent horizon of 1000-500 BCE (+2.18 to +0.79, block mean +1.43), with a declining trend across 1000-500 BCE; i.e., the PC1 value at the beginning of the period is a sharp positive spike/peak followed by a sustained drop, so 1100 BCE differs from the later horizons by being clearly, consistently and substantially higher.
payload.workflow: Loaded capital.csv (German decimal commas parsed; group/color dropped). Built 39-row x 12-variable matrix of Z-scores (symbolic: Hatchet&Swords/Dagger/HouseSize; social: CopperGold/Amber/MonumentCount; cultural: PotteryForm/PotteryDecoration; economic: Depot/Sickle/AxesCelts/MonumentSize). PCA via SVD on standardized data (center-only and YBA-only 7-slice fits as sensitivity checks); PC1 oriented so CopperGold loading is positive (higher PC1 = higher capital intensity). Extracted PC1 per 100-year slice and compared 1100 BCE vs each 1000-500 slice (pairwise differences), vs block mean/median, and internal trend of 1000-500. Cross-checked capital Z-values against time_series_data *_inter columns at slice years (0 mismatches).
